---
description: Build a one-page buyer persona from the brief and real customer quotes
---

Build a one-page buyer persona from brief/campaign-brief.md. Read the brief first; if it is missing, ask for the target audience before writing anything. If outputs/research/voice-of-customer.md exists, read it and ground the persona in its quotes.

Structure:
1. Snapshot: name, role, company size, and a two-line day-in-the-life.
2. Jobs to be done: the 3-4 functional and emotional jobs they hire a product like this for.
3. Pains: what frustrates them today, ranked by intensity.
4. Gains: what a win looks like, in concrete outcomes.
5. Watering holes: where they spend attention (communities, newsletters, podcasts, events, people they follow).
6. Objections: the top 3 reasons they would say no, each with a one-line counter.
7. Exact words: 5-8 phrases they use to describe the problem. Use verbatim quotes from voice-of-customer.md with their source when present; otherwise label them "verbatim-style, assumed".

Ground every section in the brief or a quoted source. Where both are silent, make a clearly labeled [ASSUMED] statement instead of inventing facts.
Keep it to one page: tight bullets, no filler, no em dashes.
